intro2:
It was not drawn by this app. It arrived as a Word table and was read straight into the app's own shape, then judged by the same modules that judge a design the workspace generated itself: runDesignChecks, weeklyHours, assessHardLimits, assessFatigue, scoreOrder and calcHourlyCoverage. There is no search behind it and nothing to reproduce; what can be checked is every figure on these pages.

The transcription was checksummed before anything was built on it. All 24 rows agree with the Weekly Total the document states for each, and Monday to Saturday comes to 42,000 minutes — 20 working lines × 35h to the minute. A misread digit would have shown up in both.
dutyNote: Why the duties land where they do: Monday to Saturday totals exactly 42,000 minutes — 20 × 35h to the minute — so the contract is paid. But the days are not equal: Mon 6,225 · Tue 7,205 · Wed 7,205 · Thu 7,780 · Fri 7,690 · Sat 5,895 minutes. Saturday is the lightest day and Thursday the heaviest, a spread of nearly two duties. That is a property of the design rather than a fault, and it is the first thing to put to the roster office, because it decides how much cover each day really has — the headcount rows opposite show the same story as bodies rather than minutes.
openQuestions: The four December headcounts it does not meet. Saturday opens with five where the shape asks four, and closes with three where it asks four; Sunday opens with three, not four. Saturday carries 12 people against the agreed 14, and Sunday 9 against 10. None of these is a hard limit — the design can be run exactly as written — but all four are decisions somebody made, so they need re-deciding rather than inheriting. Late-turn length. Still the reverse of the December preference: the longest late is 8h40 against a longest early of 8h30. The gap has closed to ten minutes, though, because the 9h10 Saturday closer went — so this is nearly met, where in the earlier revisions it was not close. Cover weeks. Four, which is the right number, at lines 1, 7, 12 and 17 — gaps of 8, 6, 5, 5 rather than an even six. Days worked. 4.35 a week over the 20 working lines against the 4.2 the shape names — which is EXACTLY on the tolerance the row opposite applies (0.15), and shows there as met only because binary arithmetic makes the difference a hair under it. Read it as on the line rather than either side of it. Sunday's finish — five December movements fall after 23:25, and the one duty here that runs past 8h40 is the Sunday 14:30–23:25 at 8h55; this design inherits today's window rather than deciding it.
